differences: Existing KV compressors choose tokens/budgets; Tangram makes their heterogeneous output practical in a serving system.
PagedAttention reduces request-level external fragmentation but assumes uniform head lengths; Tangram targets internal fragmentation caused by non-uniform head retention.
Jenga handles coarser layer heterogeneity and DiffKV differentiated head management; Tangram exploits cross-head retention regularity to static-plan budget, paging, and kernel partition together.
Unlike FlashDecoding static heuristics or FlashInfer runtime planning, Tangram moves partitioning fully offline using calibrated budget ratios.
limitations: Main real-system evaluation is one 4×A100 server; transfer to other GPU/CPU/multi-node systems is unproven.
2.6× headline includes underlying compression capacity gain.
Does not fix quality loss caused by the compression scorer itself.
data.implementation_status: Official aiha-lab/TANGRAM repository is public, vLLM-based and Apache-2.0. It documents installation, reproduction, ragged paging, multiple scorers, Ampere/sm_80+ requirement, and verified Qwen/Llama/Gemma/GPT-OSS models with some tensor-parallel restrictions.
data.research_positioning: KV-cache optimization/compressionとLLM servingの境界に位置するsystems paper。algorithmic evictionより、non-uniform compressionをcontinuous batching/PagedAttentionへ載せるmemory allocator・page table・scheduler・attention-kernel co-designが主題。
